entries.text:
Task: harden how toolreader displays Codex sessions, testing against the real Codex CLI sessions on this machine. Report back what you found and fixed.

Context: toolreader (this repo, read AGENTS.md first and follow it exactly, including "The ways to hurt yourself") is a read-only viewer of what coding agents did. It already lists and renders Codex sessions that ran outside T3 through `codex app-server` (src/server/CodexSessions.ts, src/core/codex.ts, src/core/normalize.ts). There are ~2600 Codex rollout files under <path>

Branch: you are on `feat/production-plan`. Create `fix/codex-display` from it and commit there. Do not touch master or push anything.

What to do:
1. Pick ~15 diverse real Codex sessions (interactive CLI, `codex exec`, long ones, ones with apply_patch / file edits, MCP tool calls, web search, failed commands, subagents, images, very large outputs, old and new rollout formats). For each, compare what the viewer shows (API `/api/threads/<id>` and the UI) against the raw rollout JSONL. Look for: missing or duplicated actions, wrong kinds/colors, wrong status (failed shown as ok), broken diffs, wrong timestamps/order, unreadable titles, items that degrade to untyped rows, crashes, slow loads.
2. Fix what is wrong, at the root cause, each with a focused unit test using a trimmed, anonymized payload (no real secrets or private paths in fixtures).
3. Known bug to fix too: shell commands quoted like '"'…'"' are parsed wrongly in src/core/shell.ts.
4. Run the server on PORT=4779 (never 4777) against a snapshot of the T3 DB as AGENTS.md "Test data" describes. Use the T3 preview browser tools to check the UI for the sessions you fixed. Stop only the server PID you started.
5. Verify: `vp test run`, `vp check`, `vp run typecheck`, `vp run build`. Commit in small conventional commits (git -c user.email=<private> commit), each ending with the line: Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

Report: a table of sessions checked (id prefix, kind, what was wrong), the commits you made, and anything you found but did not fix.

I'm adding logic to skip scripts that only call update_plan by scanning the script text for tool invocations and checking if all of them fall in the skip set, returning undefined in that case. Scripts calling tools through variables in loops should still work fine, so next I need to sweep all sessions via the API.
Now skip code-mode scripts that only update the plan:

# Fetches every listed Codex thread through the API; reports errors, slow loads, odd titles.
import json,collections,time,urllib.request,sys,concurrent.futures as cf
ids=[t['id'] for t in json.load(urllib.request.urlopen('http://127.0.0.1:4779/api/threads')) if t['source']=='codex']
def get(i):
    t=time.time()
    try: d=json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(f'http://127.0.0.1:4779/api/threads/{i}', timeout=120))
    except Exception as e: return i, None, time.time()-t, str(e)
    return i, d, time.time()-t, None
stats=collections.Counter(); titles=collections.Counter(); slow=[]; errs=[]; unsorted=[]; samples=collections.defaultdict(list)
with cf.ThreadPoolExecutor(4) as ex:
    for i,d,dt,err in ex.map(get, ids):
        if err: errs.append((i,err)); continue
        if dt>2: slow.append((i,round(dt,2)))
        es=d['entries']; ats=[e['at'] for e in es]
        if ats!=sorted(ats): unsorted.append(i)
        for e in es:
            if e['type']!='action': continue
            stats[(e['kind'],e['status'])]+=1
            head=e['title'].split(' ')[0]
            titles[(e['kind'],head)]+=1
            if len(samples[(e['kind'],head)])<2: samples[(e['kind'],head)].append((i[6:14], e['status'], e['title'][:100]))
json.dump({k[0]+'|'+k[1]:v for k,v in samples.items()}, open('<path>samples.json','w'))
print('threads',len(ids),'errors',len(errs),errs[:5]); print('slow',slow[:10]); print('unsorted',len(unsorted),unsorted[:3])
print(sorted(stats.items(), key=lambda x:-x[1])[:40])
print([ (k,v) for k,v in titles.most_common() if k[0] in ('tool','agent','web','edit')][:60])
EOF

entries.text: This session stopped abruptly without a task_complete call, so the thread is idle but would show as "running" forever since the scan only marks <private> as ended on completion. I'm thinking the fix is to check actual turn status from the thread read data instead, since turns likely carry a status like completed/interrupted/inProgress.
These are the last calls of sessions whose process died mid-call (no `task_complete`), so they'd spin forever on idle threads. Check what `thread/read` says about those turns:

entries.text: I'm figuring out how to determine if a call without output should be treated as ended, based on whether its parent turn's status is "inProgress" versus something else, and considering passing an `ended` flag into rolloutItem rather than mutating the call object directly.
`thread/read` marks those turns `interrupted`. Use the turn status: a call with no output in a turn that's no longer in progress never finished.

def rep(a,b):

    if (turn.status && turn.status !== "inProgress") finishedTurns.add(turn.id);''')
rep('''    const raw = rolloutItem(call);''','''    // A call with no output in a finished turn was cut off (e.g. Codex was killed mid-command).
    const raw = rolloutItem(call, call.ended || finishedTurns.has(call.turnId ?? ""));''')
open(p,'w').write(s)
p='src/core/rollout.ts'; s=open(p).read()

rep('''    failed || (!done && c.ended) ? "failed"''','''    failed || (!done && ended) ? "failed"''')

EOF

entries.text:
I'm noticing the tokenizer doesn't understand command substitutions like `$(...)`, which causes it to split tokens in the middle of <private> like `TOKEN=[redacted] -n 1 file)` into broken pieces rather than treating the substitution as a unit.

The fix is to make the tokenizer, when it sees `$(` or a backtick, scan forward tracking nested parens/quotes until the matching closing character, and treat that whole span as part of one word. I should also handle `command -v` cases, but shell keywords like for/do/done/fi are lower priority — I'll start by fixing command substitution and writing tests in core.test.ts.
Pre-existing tokenizer gap shows up a lot: `$(…)` command substitutions get split mid-word (`TOKEN=[redacted] -n 1 f)` → title `-n 1 f)`), and `command -v psql` shows as `-v psql`. Test first:

entries.text:
I'm adding a branch in the tokenizer so that command substitutions like `$(...)` or backtick expressions get treated as part of the current word, scanning ahead to find the matching closing character and advancing the index past it.

I also want to special-case `command -v`/`command -V` in humanizeStage so it gets labeled as a "which" lookup, inserting that check before the argument-shifting logic.
